source_basis.predecessor_source_reuse: Pure computational continuation of the predecessor's source-backed tail-floor/exact-curtailment model; no new external empirical claim introduced.

problem.terminal_action: commit iff W_r >= k among r discordant signs, with exact deterministic curtailment
problem.objective: maximize worst-position probability of committing the single q=.60 true improvement subject to all-null FWER<=.05 and q95 total-paired-observation budget

global_certificate_method.action_filter: To beat a feasible lower bound v, every used action must have raw q=.60 tail power p1>=v because prefix survival S<=1 and position power is S*p1. Any action with individual null tail p0>.05 is globally infeasible because final survival is then <.95.
global_certificate_method.multiset_enumeration: Enumerate every length-20 action-count vector from the filtered action set with product null survival >=.95 (equivalently sum -log(1-p0)<=-log(.95)).
global_certificate_method.exchange_lemma: For an action a let s_a=1-p0_a, p_a=p1_a, x_a=p_a/s_a. For adjacent a,b with x_a<=x_b, order ab has local minimum min(p_a,s_a p_b) at least order ba's min(p_b,s_b p_a), because s_b p_a<=p_a and x_a<=x_b implies s_b p_a<=s_a p_b. Later prefix survival is unchanged by the swap. Therefore sorting a multiset by increasing p1/(1-p0) gives its maximum attainable worst-position power.
global_certificate_method.order_independent_cost_necessary_bound: Let S be probability of no false commit and F_surv(B) the pair-cost CDF at B conditional on surviving all 20 null candidates. Conditional survival executes every action, so its stopped-cost convolution is permutation-invariant. For any order, total CDF(B) <= (1-S)+S*F_surv(B), obtained by optimistically assigning every false-commit path zero additional budget failure. Hence q95<=B requires this upper bound >=.95. This is a necessary, order-independent cost test.
global_certificate_method.exact_feasibility_readout: For the unique multiset surviving the power and cost necessary tests at each sampled budget, use the exchange-sorted order and compute the exact all-null stopped-cost mixture plus negative-binomial pair waiting-time mixture at rho=.20. The resulting q95 is <= budget and worst-position power equals the multiset upper bound, closing the lower/upper gap.

rho_uncertainty_extension.fixed_rho_result: For any fixed rho>=.20, the number of pairs required for a fixed discordant-sign stopping path is stochastically nonincreasing in rho; the exact q95 checks at rho .30/.40/.60 are all below the rho=.20 value.
rho_uncertainty_extension.history_varying_bound: Under the tested sign-clock model, if before observing the current discordant sign the per-pair discordance hazard is predictable and always in [.20,.60], then stagewise waiting time to each next discordance can be coupled below a Geometric(.20) wait using shared uniforms. Conditional on a realized discordant-sign stopping count d, total pair cost is therefore stochastically bounded by NegativeBinomial(d,.20). Mixing over the same sign-clock stopped-count law yields the predecessor rho=.20 cost mixture as a conservative q95 upper bound.
rho_uncertainty_extension.power_and_FWER: Under the same assumptions and eventual continuation, FWER and true-commit probabilities depend only on the discordant-sign sequence and terminal boundaries, so changing predictable discordance hazard within [.20,.60] changes pair cost but not the sign-clock error/power calculations.
rho_uncertainty_extension.scope_guard: This does not cover a discordance mechanism that depends on the current latent sign/outcome before the discordance decision, selection that changes the conditional sign law, a hazard below .20, hard pair caps that can terminate before the discordant boundary, or cross-candidate dependence outside the tested fresh-audit model.

key_results.result: At sampled q95 budgets 1800, 2000, 2500, 3000 and 3250 pairs, the previously observed feasible worst-position powers are now globally certified within the tested deterministic action class: 0.0171830, 0.0416317, 0.0430713, 0.0509520 and 0.0531186. At every point the order-independent necessary bound leaves exactly one action multiset and its exchange-sorted feasible order attains the same upper bound.

The large mid-budget mixed-depth gains are therefore not a local-search artifact at the certified points. For example budget 2000 is exactly certified at 0.0416317 versus the best fixed-depth value 0.0171830 below that budget; budget 3000 is exactly certified at 0.0509520 versus 0.0171830 fixed-depth below that budget, within the predecessor's tested comparison set.

The rho=.20 pair-cost analysis is also conservative for fixed rho in [.20,.60], and extends as a stochastic q95 upper bound to predictable history-varying discordance hazards bounded below by .20 under the stated sign-clock independence conditions.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected at the five certified budget points: the predecessor's mixed-depth frontier values might merely be local-search lower bounds. The lower and upper bounds coincide exactly under the tested deterministic tail-floor/curtailment model.
Narrowed: certification at five sampled budgets is not yet a proof of every integer-budget Pareto breakpoint from 1800 through 3300.

Narrowed: rho=.20 robustness is not arbitrary outcome-adaptive missingness robustness. The history-varying extension requires a predictable discordance hazard bounded below before the current sign is observed and preserves the conditional sign law.

Narrowed: global optimality is only inside the predecessor action class (20 candidates; r in {10,20,30,50}; exact curtailed upper-tail terminal rules; single q=.60 good candidate; all-null fresh-audit model). It does not certify stochastic within-candidate deepening or a different estimand.
